stories.headline: US launches heavy wave of strikes on Iranian targets as Middle East conflict spreads
stories.body:
US Central Command announced that it has completed a heavy wave of strikes on dozens of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets located in Iran. The military operation comes as conflict intensifies across multiple countries in the region. US Central Command stated that joint US-Saudi strikes in eastern Iraq were carried out in response to over 30 IRGC-directed aerial drone attacks during the preceding 72 hours. The US-Saudi attacks in Iraq resulted in the deaths of at least 20 members of the Iran-backed Popular Mobilisation Forces.

The strikes inside Iraq have drawn official criticism from leaders in Baghdad. Iraqi spokesperson Haider al-Aboudi stated that Baghdad has not granted any approval for attacks on specific sites or groups within Iraqi territory.

Military actions and missile exchanges extended into neighboring countries. Jordan's armed forces reported shooting down five Iranian missiles that were targeting its territory on Thursday. On the other side, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps stated that it struck the US-run Azraq base situated in Jordan. Furthermore, Iranian state media claimed that its forces destroyed several American F-35 stealth fighters operating from bases in Jordan.

Losses of life were also recorded within Iranian territories during the flare-up. Iranian state media reported that three people, including a toddler and the child's parents, were killed on Qeshm island. Iranian state media added that three IRGC members were killed in Zanjan province.

Maritime security and energy infrastructure have also been hit by the expanding violence. The government of Egypt announced that it was analysing drone fragments collected after a strike on two gas vessels in the Mediterranean port of Damietta. Meanwhile, Yemen's Houthi movement announced a blockade on Saudi ships passing through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on July 20.

Amid the rising tensions, high-level diplomatic discussions were held in an effort to contain the fighting. Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman travelled to Washington to urge restraint. During his visit, he warned against allowing the current situation to escalate into a broader regional war.

stories.headline: UEFA threatens World Cup boycott over FIFA commercial investment plan
stories.body:
European football's governing body UEFA stated on Thursday that it would boycott the World Cup if FIFA presses ahead with its private investor plan. FIFA seeks to raise up to $4.2 billion from private investors through a newly proposed commercial entity named FIFA Forward Enterprise. Under FIFA's proposal, private investors would own a 20 percent stake in FIFA Forward Enterprise. The proposed commercial subsidiary would be valued at around $20 billion, with Thrive Eternal expected to lead the proposed investor group.

To gain support, FIFA President Gianni Infantino offered member associations an increase in basic funding from $10 million to $20 million over four years if the investment proposal is approved. Infantino defended the plan by stating that FIFA Forward Enterprise is an offer, part of a democratic process, and an opportunity rather than an obligation.

However, other football bodies raised concerns. Concacaf expressed deep concerns regarding the lack of due process in FIFA's proposal, though it stopped short of calling for a boycott.

Separately, the 2030 FIFA World Cup is scheduled to be staged primarily in Spain, Portugal, and Morocco, with centenary matches in Uruguay, Argentina, and Paraguay. The Women's Under-20 World Cup in Poland is scheduled to begin on September 5.

stories.headline: Severe wildfires and extreme heat strike Southern Europe and the UK
stories.body:
A major incident was declared in the UK after a wildfire spread over more than 80 hectares on the coast of Suffolk near the Sizewell B nuclear power station. Firefighters responded to 393 wildfires across England and Wales during July, making it the busiest month on record. Additionally, Natural Resources Wales declared a drought across the whole of Wales, which is on course for its driest July in nearly 200 years.

In Southern Europe, severe wildfires caused destruction and fatalities. In France, wildfires destroyed more than 200 homes and 42,000 hectares, leaving two firefighters dead. Local authorities in France reported that a massive wildfire in the southwestern region was no longer advancing on Thursday, and France informed 84,000 evacuees in the southwest that it was safe to return home as the wildfire receded. In Greece, three firefighters died while tackling blazes, including two on the island of Crete and one in the Peloponnese region.

A study published in Scientific Reports found that the number of summer days featuring fire weather in Southern Europe has more than doubled since 1981.

stories.headline: Russian missile barrage strikes Ukraine as missile crashes in Poland
stories.body:
Russia launched a heavy barrage across Ukraine overnight. According to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Russia launched over 70 missiles and more than 280 attack drones across at least 10 Ukrainian regions. Overall, a Russian missile and drone barrage across Ukraine killed at least 10 civilians and injured more than 50 others. More than 56,000 people sheltered overnight in Kyiv's subway stations during the attack. Ukrainian air defense intercepted 55 missiles and 265 drones during the barrage.

During the strikes, a Russian ballistic missile destroyed a drone factory in Kyiv owned by Terminal Autonomy, a US corporation registered in Delaware. Terminal Autonomy manufactures AQ-400 Scythe and AQ-100 Bayonet AI-guided loitering drones in Ukraine.

The attack also spilled over near foreign borders. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk reported that an armed Russian Kh-101 cruise missile crashed near the Polish village of Tarnawa Kolonia, leaving a 10-meter-wide crater. In a previous incident, two Polish farmers were killed in November 2022 by a missile landing near the Ukrainian border, believed to be a Ukrainian air defense missile.

stories.headline: Spain sends military to Ceuta enclave following influx of migrants from Morocco
stories.body:
Spain announced it would deploy military personnel to Ceuta to support border security after hundreds of migrants entered from Morocco. Representatives from the Guardia Civil stated that between 1,500 and 2,000 migrants arrived in Ceuta over a 10-day period, representing about 2 percent of the territory's population. Ceuta regional government head Juan Jesús Vivas stated that the small city was facing a humanitarian and social emergency of national proportions. Vivas also stated that 60 bodies had been recovered at sea in recent months.

Tragedy accompanied the influx, as at least nine deaths were reported among migrants attempting to reach the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from Morocco. Earlier in the month, Spain's Supreme Court ruled that migrants intercepted at sea attempting to reach Ceuta or Melilla cannot be summarily returned to Morocco.

The situation triggered international political reactions. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called for Spain to be suspended from the Schengen zone following the migrant influx in Ceuta.

stories.headline: Indian Parliament passes strict Anti-Paper Leak Bill despite opposition walkout
stories.body:
The Parliament of India has passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026. The Rajya Sabha passed the Anti-Paper Leak Bill on Thursday, following its clearance by the Lok Sabha on Wednesday. The landmark legislation establishes strict new legal measures and severe penalties aimed at preventing fraudulent practices in public examinations across India.

During parliamentary proceedings on Thursday, the opposition demonstrated its dissatisfaction with the debate process. Opposition members belonging to the INDIA alliance walked out of the Rajya Sabha prior to the government's official reply on the Anti-Paper Leak Bill. Highlighting the extent of the issue, Congress leader Mallikarjun Kharge stated that question papers for 152 state and central examinations were leaked over the past 10 years without offenders being punished.

The amended law introduces significantly harsher prison terms and fines for convicted individuals. Under the amended law, individuals convicted of examination fraud face between five and 10 years in prison, compared with three to five years previously. Additionally, the maximum financial penalty for individual offenders under the Anti-Paper Leak Bill was increased from ₹10 lakh to ₹50 lakh.

The legislation also mandates strict penalties for institutions and organized groups involved in leaks. Service providers involved in examination fraud face fines of up to ₹5 crore and can be barred from conducting examinations for 8 years. Persons involved in organized examination crime face a minimum prison sentence of seven years and fines of up to ₹10 crore.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the passage of the new law and issued a strong warning to lawbreakers. In a video address, Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that no paper-leak mafia or gang seeking to play with the future of the nation's children will be spared.

stories.headline: Supreme Court addresses pellet gun rules as student protest row intensifies
stories.body:
The Supreme Court of India directed the Delhi government to provide medical treatment to students injured during protests at Jantar Mantar. Addressing police action, the Supreme Court declined to issue a blanket ban on pellet guns for crowd control, noting police regulations permit their use in exceptional situations.

The developments follow police action during a recent demonstration. Delhi Police registered 13 FIRs and identified over 2,800 individuals with criminal backgrounds in connection with the July 20 protest march. A legal aid helpline set up for student protesters received 300 calls, including 50 from young women reporting rape and death threats.

Political fallout from the protests continues. The Delhi government issued an order directing that no further action be taken on FIRs filed against Cockroach Janta Party protesters. However, CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das stated that the Delhi government should formally withdraw FIRs against student protesters rather than marking them as closed. Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke demanded the resignation of Union Home Minister Amit Shah over police action during the July 20 protest. Meanwhile, Pralhad Joshi was appointed as India's new Education Minister following the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET exam paper leak controversy.

stories.headline: PM Modi chairs high-level security meeting on West Asia crisis and supply chains
stories.body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired the fourth special meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Security to review the West Asia crisis and supply chains. During the meeting, PM Modi directed the establishment of a mechanism to provide emergency assistance, timely information, and counselling to Indian seafarers and their families.

The decision comes amid growing risks to Indian citizens in the region. The Indian government informed Parliament that 16 Indian nationals, including 10 seafarers, have lost their lives in the Middle East conflict this year. An additional 12 Indian nationals died in an accidental explosion at a gas facility in Qatar in June. More than 10 million Indian nationals reside and work in West Asia, primarily in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

The conflict also threatens energy security and shipping. Prior to recent conflict escalations, 40 percent of India's energy imports passed through the Strait of Hormuz. Furthermore, India relies on foreign imports to meet over 88 percent of its total energy requirements. Ship crossings through the Bab al-Mandeb Strait fell from an average of 43 per day in early July to 31 per day following Houthi targeting threats.

stories.headline: India warns Ukraine and Russia over Black Sea attacks on commercial ships
stories.body:
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar stated to Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha that attacks on commercial shipping and Indian seafarers in the Black Sea are absolutely unacceptable. Five Indian seafarers have died and two remain missing following recent attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea by Russian and Ukrainian forces.

Tensions over shipping casualties have led to formal diplomatic protests. India summoned Ukrainian Ambassador Oleksandr Polishchuk on July 27 to protest a strike on the merchant vessel M.V. Omorfi that killed an Indian sailor. A Russian projectile attack on the M.V. Golden Leo off Odesa on July 19 killed 10 seafarers, including four Indian nationals. India summoned Russian Chargé d'Affaires Vladimir Ladanov on July 22 to convey grave concern over the deadly strike on M.V. Golden Leo.

Meanwhile, Indian sailors remain at risk in Ukrainian ports. Thirteen Indian seafarers are stranded on board a foreign-flagged vessel in the Ukrainian port of Chornomorsk amid Russian drone and missile strikes. The Indian Embassy in Ukraine reported monitoring the merchant vessel MV AMIR1, which carries 13 Indian crew members, amid repeated missile and drone threats.
